note: NASA names a region for each planned delivery and gives no coordinates. The places below are where this tool searches for landing areas; they are not announced landing sites.

deliveries.detail: NASA's release 26-046 of 2026-05-26 says the Blue Moon Mark 1 lander of Moon Base I, carrying two payloads, will "land on the Shackleton Connecting Ridge". That it is this delivery (the same lander, two payloads) is inferred.

mouton.name: Mons Mouton
mouton.basis: The Artemis III candidate region "Mons Mouton" already in the catalogue (USGS outline); the map shows 96 km around its centre.

ridge.name: Shackleton connecting ridge
ridge.basis: Constructed for this tool, not published by NASA: the point midway between the rims of Shackleton (centre -89.67, 129.78, diameter 20.92 km) and de Gerlache (centre -88.48, -88.34, diameter 32.71 km), from the IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, features 5450 and 1439 (read 2026-11-15). The rims are 27.5 km apart; the map shows 96 km around the point.

pole.name: South pole, 75-90 S
pole.basis: NASA says only "lunar south pole": the whole polar map is searched.
